title: What are the JPA inheritance strategies SINGLE_TABLE, JOINED, and TABLE_PER_CLASS? How does each map tables, and what are the trade-offs?
keyPoints: SINGLE_TABLE (default): one table with a discriminator column -- fastest queries, but subtype columns must be nullable
JOINED: base table plus one table per subclass joined by shared primary key -- normalized, but every read pays a join cost
TABLE_PER_CLASS: each concrete class gets a full standalone table -- simple per type, but polymorphic queries require UNION ALL
Default to SINGLE_TABLE for performance when subtype NOT NULL constraints are not critical
Choose JOINED when data integrity matters and subtype-specific columns must be NOT NULL
Avoid TABLE_PER_CLASS unless subtypes are queried in isolation and polymorphic queries are rare
Switching strategy later is a schema migration, so decide early based on query patterns and integrity needs

s1_definition.oneliner: SINGLE_TABLE stores the whole hierarchy in one table with a discriminator column; JOINED normalizes into base plus per-subclass tables joined by key; TABLE_PER_CLASS gives each concrete class a full standalone table.
s1_definition.profdef:
When you use @Inheritance for an entity hierarchy, JPA offers three strategies for table layout.

- **SINGLE_TABLE** – stores all subtypes in one table with a discriminator column identifying each row's type; subtype-specific columns are nullable because they do not apply to every row.
- **JOINED** – gives the base class its own table and each subclass its own table holding only its extra columns, linked by a shared primary key; loading a subtype requires a JOIN.
- **TABLE_PER_CLASS** – gives each concrete subclass its own complete table including all inherited columns; there is no shared base table, so polymorphic queries must UNION ALL across all subclass tables.
- **@DiscriminatorColumn** – defines the column in a SINGLE_TABLE strategy that identifies which subclass each row belongs to.
- **@DiscriminatorValue** – specifies the value stored in the discriminator column for a particular subclass.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, imagine storing savings and current account records. SINGLE_TABLE is one giant ledger book where every account is a row with a "type" stamp and some columns left blank when they do not apply -- fast to read, but messy with blanks. JOINED is a main ledger for common details plus a separate thin booklet for savings-only details and another for current-only details, cross-referenced by account number -- tidy with no blanks, but you flip between books (join) to see everything. TABLE_PER_CLASS is two entirely separate complete ledgers, one for savings and one for current, each self-contained -- simple per type, but "list all accounts" means reading both books and stitching them together.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  SINGLE_TABLE:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                     accounts table                       │
  ├────────────┬──────────────┬─────────┬───────┬────────────┤
  │ account_id │ account_type │ balance │ rate  │ overdraft  │
  │ (PK)       │ (discriminator)        │(SAV)  │ (CUR)      │
  ├────────────┼──────────────┼─────────┼───────┼────────────┤
  │ SAV2001    │ SAVINGS      │ 50000   │ 6.50  │ NULL       │
  │ CUR3001    │ CURRENT      │ 120000  │ NULL  │ 50000      │
  └────────────┴──────────────┴─────────┴───────┴────────────┘
  (one table, discriminator, nullable subtype columns)
```

```text
  JOINED:
  ┌────────────────────────────┐
  │     accounts (base)        │
  │ account_id │ holder │ bal  │
  │ SAV2001    │ Priya  │50000 │
  │ CUR3001    │ Rajesh │120k  │
  └─────┬──────────────┬───────┘
        │ JOIN         │ JOIN
        ▼              ▼
  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐
  │savings_accts │ │current_accts     │
  │ account_id   │ │ account_id       │
  │ interest_rate│ │ overdraft_limit  │
  │ SAV2001│6.50 │ │ CUR3001│50000    │
  └──────────────┘ └──────────────────┘
  (base + subclass tables, joined by PK)
```

```text
  TABLE_PER_CLASS:
  ┌────────────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────┐
  │   savings_accounts         │  │   current_accounts          │
  │ id│acct_id│holder│bal│rate │  │ id│acct_id│holder│bal│limit │
  │ 1 │SAV2001│Priya │50k│6.50│  │ 2 │CUR3001│Rajesh│120k│50k  │
  └────────────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────────┘
  (separate complete tables, no shared base table)
  Polymorphic query = UNION ALL of both tables
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
When you use @Inheritance for an entity hierarchy, JPA gives you three strategies that each lay out the database differently. SINGLE_TABLE, the default, stores the whole hierarchy in one table with a discriminator column identifying each row's type. Subtype-specific columns are nullable because they do not apply to every row. It is the fastest because queries need no joins, but subtype-only columns cannot have NOT NULL constraints at the database level.

JOINED normalizes the model by giving the base class a table with common columns and each subclass its own table with only its extra columns, linked by a primary key that is also a foreign key. This enforces NOT NULL on subtype columns because they live in their own tables, but every read pays a join cost, and polymorphic queries join across all subclass tables. TABLE_PER_CLASS gives each concrete subclass its own complete standalone table with all inherited columns, so a single-subtype read has no join, but polymorphic queries require UNION ALL across every table, which is slow, and IDENTITY id generation does not work because ids must be unique across the union.

At National Bank of India, Pankaj chooses based on query patterns and integrity needs. The account hierarchy uses SINGLE_TABLE because accounts are read constantly and polymorphically, and the join cost of JOINED would hurt, accepting a couple of nullable subtype columns. The loan product hierarchy uses JOINED because each loan type has many required subtype-specific fields that need NOT NULL constraints. TABLE_PER_CLASS is reserved for the rare case where subtypes are queried in isolation and polymorphic queries are nearly nonexistent.

Remember one sentence: SINGLE_TABLE is fastest with one table and a discriminator; JOINED is normalized with a join per read; TABLE_PER_CLASS is standalone tables with UNION ALL for polymorphic queries.
